items.title: The induction step from property V-n to property V-n-plus-one in the comparison of topologies

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the induction step (V_n) implies (V_{n+1}) in the comparison of two topologies on a site carrying the data of the situation, namely a set of arrows P and weak Serre subcategories A'_X of the tau'-sheaves (statement lines 7147-7150, with the situation delivered verbatim as a context span from lines 6840-6879). The proof has four stages: an arbitrary class in degree n+1 is replaced, using locality of cohomology, by the target of an arrow of P that is a tau-covering (proof lines 7152-7172); the degree-n comparison result produces the corresponding tau'-class and the induction hypothesis kills it locally after pullback along an arrow of P (proof lines 7184-7194); finally the hypothesis that the class dies under the canonical map F -> Rf_{tau,*}f_tau^{-1}F, together with the cited Leray-type lemma and a distinguished-triangle argument, kills the original class on a tau'-covering, which is the assertion (proof lines 7205-7289). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping that lets the degree-n statement be applied to the twisted data and then lifted back. The claim is H2: a long reduction, written out in full, with each step attributed to a named result of the same section.
